problems.title: The released foresight routine does not execute its requested DDIM interval under the checked dependency
problems.source_location: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1, arXiv v1 PDF p. 5; current foresight_sampling_update and Diffusers DDIM/InverseDDIM step methods.
claim: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 define a selected forward-and-return interval. The current author routine assigns a custom timestep array before calling standard DDIM schedulers. Both the historical dependency examined and the latest Diffusers source instead select coefficients by the configured global stride.
analysis: With \(1000\) training steps and \(40\) inference steps, that stride is \(25\). A forward call at \(975\) uses \(950\), even when the custom array requests \(850\); the inverse call at \(850\) uses coefficients for \(825\to850\). Consequently the requested \(975\to850\to975\) interval is not executed, even with deterministic zero noise prediction. This is a scheduler-endpoint mismatch, not a general claim of exact reversibility for learned diffusion.

For a deterministic zero noise field, \(x=1\) and \(\bar\alpha_t=[1+(t/1000)^2]^{-1}\), the intended forward value is \(1.0641608508\), versus \(1.0125688439\) for the actual coefficient pair. The resulting mismatched round trip is \(1.0001850408\), while explicit reversed endpoints cancel to \(1\). This is direct arithmetic, with no image-generation claim.
result: Latest scheduler source still ignores the substituted endpoint array for these coefficient choices; the release/algorithm discrepancy does not refute the abstract fixed-point construction or quantify image quality.
repair: Use a DDIM operator with both coefficient endpoints passed explicitly. This local reformulation does not establish improved image-benchmark scores.
